questions.question:
How many of the following species have all the σ-bond forming orbitals of central atom with equal p-character.
$\nSF$6<\/sub> , , PH3<\/sub> , CO2<\/sub> , C$\u$2113F3 <\/sub>, , , SF4<\/sub> <\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
**Question Explanation: Identifying species with equal p-character in all σ-bond forming orbitals.
$ $
$ $**Concept: Orbital Hybridization Symmetry.
$ $
$ $**Solution: Orbitals have **equal p-character only if the hybridization is "pure" (like sp,sp2,sp3,sp3d2) and there are **no lone pairs on the central atom that cause distortions, or if the geometry is perfectly symmetrical (all terminal atoms are same).$ $
    $ $
  • **SF6$\u$200b, IF6+$\u$200b, PH4+$\u$200b, NO2+$\u$200b: These have regular geometries (Octahedral, Octahedral, Tetrahedral, Linear respectively) with no lone pairs on the central atom. All σ-orbitals are equivalent.
    • $ $
  • **CO2: Carbon is sp hybridized with no lone pairs; both σ-orbitals are equivalent.
    • $ $
  • **ClF3, SF4$\u$200b: These have lone pairs on the central atom, which causes the p-character to be distributed unequally between lone pair orbitals and bond orbitals.
    • $ $
$ However$ in PH3, the three p-H bonds are formed using almost pure 3p orbitals. So, all three bonds use equivalent p-orbital.
$ Species$ with equal p-character: SF6,$\u$200b,CO2$\u$200b,NO2+$\u$200b,PH4+$\u$200b, PH3 Total count = 6.
$ $
$ $**Final Answer: 6

questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which of the following is correct for critical temperature?<\/div>$\n$
options: It is the highest temperature at which liquid and vapour can coexist.
Beyond this temperature, there is no distinction between the two phases and a gas cannot be liquefied by compression.
At this temperature, the surface tension of the system is zero.
At this temperature, the gas and the liquid phases have different critical densities.
questions.explanation:
$ $ **Question Explanation:
$ Identify$ the correct statements defining critical temperature.
$ $
$ $**Concept:
$ This$ question is based on Critical Temperature (TC) and the Critical Point.
$ $
$ $**Solution:
$ Statement$ 1: The critical temperature is indeed the highest temperature on the liquid-vapour coexistence curve. Above this temperature, the substance cannot exist as a liquid, regardless of pressure. This statement is correct.
$ Statement$ 2: Beyond the critical temperature, the substance enters the supercritical fluid state, where the distinct properties of liquid and gas phases (like density, surface tension) no longer exist. The primary definition of TC is the temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied simply by increasing pressure. This statement is correct.
$ Statement$ 3: Surface tension is a property of the interface between a liquid and its vapour. At the critical point (which occurs at TC and PC), the densities and all other properties of the liquid and vapour phases become identical. Since there is no longer a distinct interface, the surface tension becomes zero. This statement is correct.
$ Statement$ 4: At the critical point (at TC), the liquid and gas phases merge into a single phase. Their densities become identical, not different. This specific density is known as the critical density. This statement is false.
$ $
$ $**Final Answer: The correct option is (1), (2) and (3).
